report.summary: One test failed: the blank-title case of test_invalid_book_is_rejected got 201 instead of 422. The app's validate_book skips the blank-title check whenever the blank_title seeded bug is enabled via the BUGS env var, and this run's failure pattern points to that bug being on. Treat it as the expected product defect: confirm whether BUGS=blank_title is meant to be set for this run, and if it is a real regression, fix the check at app/main.py:86.

causes.title: API accepts a book with a whitespace-only title
causes.explanation: validate_book only raises the 422 'Title must not be blank' when the stripped title is empty AND 'blank_title' is not in BUGS (app/main.py:86). With BUGS containing blank_title, the blank-title check is skipped entirely, so POST /api/books with title '   ' is stored and returns 201. The test asserts the correct behaviour (422 with the message), so the test is right to fail. The other three parametrised cases (empty-author, next-year, year-zero) passed, which fits a single seeded bug being active rather than a broken test. The workflow file (.github/workflows/tests.yml) does not set BUGS, so the flag must come from the CI environment; the repo alone does not prove that.
evidence: app/main.py:86: if not book.title.strip() and "blank_title" not in BUGS:
app/main.py:10: blank_title      accepts a title made only of spaces
app/main.py:31: BUGS = {b.strip() for b in os.environ.get("BUGS", "").split(",") if b.strip()}
Run totals: tests=26, failures=1, errors=0, skipped=0; only the blank-title case failed.
causes.suggested_fix: First, check the CI environment for BUGS=blank_title. If the seeded bug should be off for this run, unset it and rerun. If the bug is meant to be on, mark this case as an expected failure (xfail) with a reason pointing to the seeded bug, so the suite stays green and still tracks it. If it is a real regression, change app/main.py:86 so the blank-title check does not depend on the blank_title flag: if not book.title.strip(): raise HTTPException(422, 'Title must not be blank').
